experiences.name: Mercado de San Juan Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of Mexico City's most beloved gourmet markets, sampling exotic cheeses, fresh seafood tostadas, traditional tacos, and artisanal products. Chat with local vendors and taste authentic Mexican ingredients rarely found elsewhere.

experiences.name: Teotihuacan Pyramids & Street Food
experiences.description: Visit the ancient pre-Aztec city of Teotihuacan, climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Moon, and explore the Avenue of the Dead. On the way back, stop at a roadside pulque bar and try traditional tlayudas and barbacoa from local vendors.

experiences.name: Coyoacán Neighborhood & Frida Kahlo Museum
experiences.description: Wander the cobblestone streets of bohemian Coyoacán, visit the iconic Casa Azul (Frida Kahlo Museum), browse artisan crafts at Mercado de Artesanías, and enjoy a traditional Mexican lunch at a local cantina with pozole or enchiladas.

experiences.name: Tacos & Mezcal Evening in Roma Norte
experiences.description: Join locals on a self-guided taco crawl through Roma Norte, one of the city's hippest neighborhoods. Sample tacos al pastor, suadero, and carnitas from legendary street stands, then wind down with a flight of artisanal mezcal at a traditional mezcalería.

experiences.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes & Historic Center Walk
experiences.description: Admire the stunning Art Nouveau exterior of the Palacio de Bellas Artes and explore its world-class murals by Diego Rivera and David Alfaro Siqueiros inside. Stroll through the Zócalo, visit the Metropolitan Cathedral, and explore the ancient Templo Mayor ruins.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 13:00. Use the morning to rest on the plane and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at AIFA or Benito Juárez Airport, take the Metro (Line 1, ~5 MXN) or a pre-paid airport taxi (~150–200 MXN) to Centro Histórico. Check in to the boutique stay, freshen up, then take a relaxed first walk around the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución) – one of the largest city squares in the world. Admire the Metropolitan Cathedral and the National Palace exterior, both free to view from outside.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Calle Regina, a lively pedestrian street in Centro Histórico full of street food vendors and local life. Explore the area around Mercado de San Juan Arcos de Belén for a feel of local evening culture.

meals.lunch: Grab a quick and cheap meal at a street taco stand near the Zócalo upon arrival. Look for tacos de canasta or tacos al pastor (~15–25 MXN per taco).
meals.dinner: Eat at a comedor (small local eatery) on Calle Regina. Try a set menu 'comida corrida' style dinner – soup, main dish, and agua fresca for ~80–120 MXN.

day_by_day.notes: Keep luggage light and secure on public transit. Get a rechargeable Metro card (tarjeta) at the airport Metro station for easy travel all week. Exchange a small amount of cash at the airport or use a fee-free ATM in Centro.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a hearty breakfast near the hotel, then head to the Templo Mayor archaeological site (entry ~80 MXN, free on Sundays). This ancient Aztec temple ruin sits right next to the Zócalo and includes an excellent on-site museum. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the ruins and artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Palacio Nacional (National Palace) on the Zócalo's east side – entry is FREE. Marvel at Diego Rivera's stunning murals depicting Mexican history along the grand staircase. Afterward, visit the Plaza de Santo Domingo nearby and watch traditional scribes (evangelistas) at their typewriters – a unique cultural sight.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Mercado de Artesanías La Ciudadela (~15-min walk or short Metro ride) to browse affordable local crafts and souvenirs. Then enjoy the vibrant nightlife atmosphere around Alameda Central park.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a local market breakfast spot near Centro – chilaquiles or tamales with atole from a street vendor (~40–60 MXN).
meals.lunch: Try a traditional comida corrida at a family-run restaurant near Templo Mayor (~80–100 MXN for a full 3-course meal with drink).
meals.dinner: Visit Mercado de San Juan (Mercado Internacional) for affordable fresh food stalls – try a tlayuda or enfrijoladas (~60–90 MXN).

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor is closed on Mondays, so Tuesday is perfect. Wear comfortable walking shoes – you'll cover 4–6 km on foot today. Carry water as March can be warm and dry.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro (Line 2) to Bellas Artes station. Visit the Palacio de Bellas Artes – the exterior and ground floor murals are FREE to view. Then walk through Alameda Central, Mexico City's oldest public park. Continue to the Museo Mural Diego Rivera (entry ~45 MXN) to see Rivera's famous 'Dream of a Sunday Afternoon in Alameda Park' mural up close.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Metro to the Coyoacán neighborhood (Line 3 to Viveros or Coyoacán station, ~5 MXN). Explore the colorful Jardín Hidalgo and Jardín Centenario plazas, then visit the Mercado de Coyoacán for snacks and local goods. Walk to the Casa Azul – Frida Kahlo Museum (entry ~270 MXN, book online in advance to guarantee entry).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the bohemian atmosphere of Coyoacán in the evening. Street performers and local vendors fill the plazas. Head back to Centro via Metro.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh-baked pastries (pan dulce) and coffee from a local panadería near your hotel (~20–30 MXN).
meals.lunch: Eat at the Mercado de Coyoacán – try a tostada de tinga or a pozole bowl from one of the market stalls (~50–80 MXN).
meals.dinner: Back in Centro, try a torta (Mexican sandwich) from a popular torta shop near the hotel (~50–70 MXN) with a fresh-squeezed juice.

day_by_day.notes: Book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets online at least a few days ahead – they sell out fast. Coyoacán is very walkable and safe for tourists. Keep an eye on your belongings on the Metro during rush hour.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Teotihuacán – the ancient Pyramid city. Catch an early bus from the Terminal Central del Norte (Metro Line 5 to Autobuses del Norte, then Autobuses Teotihuacán bus, ~50 MXN round trip). Arrive early to beat crowds and heat. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon (site entry ~90 MXN). Walk the Avenue of the Dead and explore the Temple of Quetzalcóatl.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Teotihuacán's lesser-visited areas like the Palace of Quetzalpapálotl. Browse local vendors selling obsidian crafts outside the site. Head back to Mexico City by early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico. Rest briefly, then explore the Barrio Chino (Chinatown) on Calle Dolores – a quirky, compact cultural curiosity just minutes from your hotel. End the evening with a walk through the illuminated Zócalo at night.

meals.breakfast: Eat before leaving – grab atole and tamales from an early-morning street vendor near the hotel (~30–40 MXN).
meals.lunch: Pack snacks or eat at one of the simple comedores just outside the Teotihuacán site entrance – quesadillas and agua fresca (~70–100 MXN).
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a sit-down dinner at a mid-range traditional Mexican restaurant in Centro – mole enchiladas or chiles en nogada (~120–160 MXN).

day_by_day.notes: Leave by 7:30–8:00 AM to arrive at Teotihuacán when it opens at 9:00 AM. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water – the site is fully exposed with little shade. Wear very comfortable shoes for the pyramid climbs.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mercado de la Merced – one of the largest traditional markets in Latin America, just a short Metro ride from Centro. Wander through its enormous stalls selling spices, chiles, fresh produce, street food, and everything imaginable. A true immersive local cultural experience that is completely free to enter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or Metro to the Museo Nacional de Arte (MUNAL) near Alameda Central (entry ~70 MXN, free on Sundays). Explore Mexican fine art from the colonial era to the 20th century across its stunning neoclassical building. Afterward, stroll through the historic streets of Centro one last time – visit the Casa de los Azulejos (House of Tiles), a beautiful 18th-century building now housing a Sanborns café.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Mexico City – spend it at a pulquería (traditional pulque bar) near Centro for a truly local experience. Pulque (fermented agave drink) is very affordable (~25–40 MXN per cup). End the night with street tacos from your favorite vendor discovered during the trip.

meals.breakfast: Eat at Mercado de la Merced – fresh fruit with chili and lime, or a gordita with beans and cheese (~30–50 MXN).
meals.lunch: Comida corrida at a local restaurant near MUNAL – soup, rice, main dish, and drink (~90–110 MXN).
meals.dinner: Street tacos farewell dinner – al pastor, suadero, or barbacoa tacos from a trusted street stand in Centro (~15–25 MXN each, order 3–4 tacos).

day_by_day.notes: La Merced market is best visited in the morning when it's most active. Keep valuables secure in busy markets. Use your remaining pesos on food and small souvenirs. Check out time and any onward travel arrangements should be confirmed the night before.

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Check in to your boutique hotel in Centro Histórico, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely walk to the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest city squares in the world. Explore the exterior of the Metropolitan Cathedral and admire the National Palace facade with its famous Diego Rivera murals visible from the courtyard. Stroll through the surrounding streets to soak in the colonial architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Templo Mayor archaeological site area for a golden-hour atmosphere, then explore the pedestrian street Madero. Wind down with a mezcal tasting at a local cantina near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: El Cardenal (Palma 23, Centro Histórico) — a beloved mid-range institution serving classic Mexican cuisine; try the tamales or enchiladas verdes.
meals.dinner: Café de Tacuba — a historic restaurant open since 1912 near the hotel; enjoy mole dishes and traditional Mexican comfort food in a stunning tiled dining room.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light since you arrive at 13:00. Focus on getting comfortable in the neighborhood. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance. Exchange some currency or use ATMs near the Zócalo.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Templo Mayor Museum (opens 9:00 AM) — the excavated Aztec temple complex right in the heart of Centro Histórico. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the ruins and the excellent museum showcasing pre-Hispanic artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Palacio de Bellas Artes to admire its stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture and view the Diego Rivera, Orozco, and Siqueiros murals inside. Afterward, explore the nearby Alameda Central park for a relaxing stroll among locals.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Barrio Chino (Chinatown) area or explore the Correo Mayor street. Visit the Palacio Postal (Postal Palace) if still open, then enjoy a vibrant evening in a nearby pulquería for a traditional pulque experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a nearby café — try a classic Mexican desayuno with chilaquiles, fresh juice, and café de olla at Café El Popular (5 de Mayo street, open 24 hrs).
meals.lunch: Mercado de San Juan — a mid-range gourmet market a short walk from Bellas Artes; sample fresh seafood tostadas, artisan cheeses, and Mexican charcuterie at the market stalls.
meals.dinner: Azul Histórico (Isabel la Católica 30) — an elegant but mid-range courtyard restaurant specializing in regional Mexican cuisine; try the mole negro or chiles en nogada (seasonal).

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor is closed on Mondays. Bellas Artes hosts ballet folklórico performances on Sundays and Wednesdays — check the schedule and book tickets in advance if interested (~$15–25 USD).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Teotihuacán — take an early bus from Terminal Norte (accessible by Metro from Centro) for about a 1-hour ride. Spend the morning climbing the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon and walking the Avenue of the Dead. Arrive early to beat crowds and heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mexico City by early afternoon. Rest briefly at the hotel, then visit the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec Park (take the Metro to Auditorio or Chapultepec station) — one of the world's greatest anthropology museums housing the Aztec Sun Stone.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the trendy Condesa or Roma Norte neighborhood for an evening stroll. Browse boutique shops and enjoy the Art Deco architecture before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — grab fresh fruit, tamales, or tortas from street vendors near the hotel or at the bus terminal.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Teotihuacán — eat at one of the on-site restaurants such as La Gruta, a restaurant inside a natural cave near the pyramids (mid-range, atmospheric, and worth the experience).
meals.dinner: Contramar or a similar seafood spot in Roma Norte — try the famous tuna tostadas and grilled fish; budget ~$20–30 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes and sunscreen for Teotihuacán — it involves significant walking and climbing. Bring water. Buses to Teotihuacán depart every 30 minutes from Terminal Norte. The site opens at 9:00 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Coyoacán neighborhood — take the Metro (Line 3 to Viveros or Coyoacán station). Explore the charming colonial streets, the main plaza (Jardín Centenario), and the iconic Frida Kahlo Museum (La Casa Azul). Book tickets online in advance as they sell out quickly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Leon Trotsky Museum (Casa de Trotsky) for a fascinating historical detour. Then browse the Mercado de Artesanías de Coyoacán for unique local crafts, textiles, and souvenirs at mid-range prices.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico. Explore the nightlife around República de Uruguay and Regina streets — a lively pedestrian zone with bars, live music, and street food vendors that comes alive after dark.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Coyoacán at Café El Jarocho — a legendary local coffee spot with fresh-brewed café de olla and pastries; expect a line but it moves fast.
meals.lunch: Mercado de Coyoacán food stalls — try tostadas de tinga, enchiladas, or fresh aguas frescas from the market vendors inside the covered market (very affordable and authentic).
meals.dinner: Los Danzantes (Jardín Centenario 12, Coyoacán) — a stylish mid-range restaurant and mezcalería with excellent Mexican cuisine and a fantastic mezcal selection; try the duck in mole.

day_by_day.notes: Frida Kahlo Museum tickets must be booked well in advance online at museofridakahlo.org.mx — walk-in tickets are rarely available. Coyoacán is very walkable once you arrive. The neighborhood is especially lively on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mercado de la Merced or Mercado Jamaica for an immersive local market experience — one of the largest traditional markets in Latin America. Watch vendors, sample street food, and observe everyday Mexico City life. Then stop by the nearby Museo de la Ciudad de México (City Museum) for a quick cultural overview.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Zócalo area for any last-minute sights you may have missed — consider the interior of the National Palace to see Diego Rivera's epic murals up close (free entry with ID). Visit a local chocolate or artisan shop on Calle Mesones for edible souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Centro Histórico. Pack your bags and enjoy a relaxed final evening.

meals.breakfast: Street breakfast near the hotel — huevos a la mexicana, fresh-squeezed orange juice, and pan dulce from a local panadería on 5 de Mayo or Madero street.
meals.lunch: La Opera Bar (Cinco de Mayo 10) — a historic cantina-style restaurant with bullet holes allegedly from Pancho Villa in the ceiling; enjoy classic Mexican dishes in a stunning Belle Époque interior.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Limosneros (Allende 3, Centro Histórico) — a creative mid-range restaurant celebrating pre-Hispanic and regional Mexican ingredients with modern technique; excellent cocktails using native spirits.

day_by_day.notes: Check your departure flight time and arrange airport transfer in advance. Mexico City traffic can be heavy — allow at least 1.5–2 hours to reach the airport during peak hours. Keep some pesos for tips and last-minute purchases.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Mexico City International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private chauffeur transfer to boutique hotel in Centro Histórico. Check-in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity at the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely orientation walk through the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest city squares in the world. Visit the stunning Metropolitan Cathedral (Catedral Metropolitana) and admire its baroque façade. Stroll along Calle Madero, a pedestrian street lined with colonial architecture, stopping at the Casa de los Azulejos (House of Tiles) for a quick look at its iconic Talavera-tiled exterior.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset visit to the rooftop terrace bar of a nearby luxury hotel overlooking the Zócalo for cocktails and panoramic views. Dinner at Azul Histórico, a celebrated restaurant set in a beautiful colonial courtyard in Centro Histórico, renowned for elevated traditional Mexican cuisine.

meals.lunch: Light welcome lunch at the hotel restaurant or a nearby upscale café such as Café de Tacuba, a historic institution serving classic Mexican dishes since 1912.
meals.dinner: Azul Histórico — signature dishes include mole negro, chiles en nogada (seasonal), and artisanal mezcal cocktails. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel. Confirm hotel concierge has arranged all upcoming reservations. Tip: The Zócalo is beautifully lit at night — a short after-dinner stroll is highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Templo Mayor archaeological site, the ancient Aztec temple unearthed in the heart of Centro Histórico. Includes the adjacent Templo Mayor Museum, home to extraordinary pre-Columbian artifacts including the famous Coyolxauhqui stone disc. Hire a specialized archaeologist guide for an in-depth experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Palacio Nacional (National Palace) to view Diego Rivera's sweeping murals depicting the history of Mexico — an unmissable cultural masterpiece. Afterward, explore the nearby Mercado de Artesanías or browse high-end craft galleries on República de Uruguay street for authentic Mexican art and textiles.
day_by_day.evening: Private mezcal and tequila tasting experience at a curated mezcalería in Centro Histórico, such as La Botica or Expendio de Maíz Sin Nombre, guided by a spirits sommelier. Follow with dinner at Pujol (arrange private car transfer — approximately 20 minutes), consistently ranked among the world's top restaurants, offering an iconic tasting menu centered on corn and ancient Mexican culinary traditions.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel — request a traditional Mexican spread with chilaquiles, tamales, fresh fruit, and café de olla.
meals.lunch: El Cardenal, a legendary fine-dining institution in Centro Histórico celebrated for its traditional Mexican breakfast and lunch menus, including handmade tortillas and seasonal specialties.
meals.dinner: Pujol — Chef Enrique Olvera's tasting menu (8–10 courses). Book weeks in advance. Signature dish: Mole Madre, an aged mole with over 1,000 days of continuous cooking.

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor opens at 9:00 AM. Palacio Nacional is free but may have queues — a private guide will help bypass delays. Confirm Pujol reservation well in advance as it books out quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Private full-day excursion to Teotihuacán, the ancient pre-Aztec city of pyramids, located approximately 50 km northeast of the city (45-minute private car ride). Arrive early to beat crowds. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon, walk the Avenue of the Dead, and explore the Temple of Quetzalcóatl. Hire a certified archaeologist guide for a premium, in-depth experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Teotihuacán, including the Palace of Tepantitla with its vibrant murals. Optional: private hot air balloon flight over the pyramids at sunrise (arrange for an early 6:00 AM departure variation if preferred). Return to Centro Histórico by mid-afternoon. Freshen up at the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Palacio de Bellas Artes (Palace of Fine Arts), Mexico City's premier cultural venue, to admire its stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture and the murals inside by Rivera, Orozco, and Siqueiros. Check the evening program for a ballet folklórico performance or classical concert. Dinner nearby at a premium restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — request a packed gourmet picnic basket from the hotel to enjoy at Teotihuacán.
meals.lunch: Private catered lunch among the pyramids arranged through a luxury tour operator, or dine at La Gruta, a dramatic restaurant set inside a natural cave adjacent to the archaeological zone.
meals.dinner: Limosneros, a celebrated restaurant in Centro Histórico offering creative contemporary Mexican cuisine with pre-Hispanic ingredients, set in a stunning 16th-century colonial space.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes and sun protection for Teotihuacán — the site is expansive and exposed. Carry water. The Bellas Artes murals are viewable during the day; evening performances require advance tickets.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the historic neighborhood of Coyoacán (30-minute private car transfer). Visit the Casa Azul — the Frida Kahlo Museum — one of Mexico City's most iconic cultural landmarks, showcasing the artist's life, work, and personal belongings. Book skip-the-line premium tickets in advance. Explore the charming cobblestone streets and colonial plazas of Coyoacán afterward.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Leon Trotsky Museum, adjacent to Coyoacán, for a fascinating historical perspective. Browse the upscale Bazar Artesanal in Coyoacán's central market for premium crafts, textiles, and folk art. Transfer to the trendy Polanco neighborhood for luxury shopping along Presidente Masaryk Avenue — Mexico City's equivalent of the Champs-Élysées — with flagship stores and local designer boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktail hour at a rooftop bar in Polanco with views over the city. Dinner at Quintonil, another world-renowned restaurant by Chef Jorge Vallejo, celebrated for its contemporary interpretation of Mexican ingredients and techniques — consistently ranked among Latin America's best restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — try huevos motuleños or enfrijoladas for an authentic Mexican morning experience.
meals.lunch: El Hijo del Cuervo in Coyoacán, a beloved bohemian restaurant with a beautiful terrace, serving elevated Mexican comfort food and craft beers in a lively cultural atmosphere.
meals.dinner: Quintonil, Polanco — seasonal tasting menu highlighting native Mexican ingredients such as huitlacoche, epazote, and chapulines. Pair with a curated Mexican wine or mezcal flight.

day_by_day.notes: Frida Kahlo Museum requires advance reservations — premium time slots sell out weeks ahead. Coyoacán is best explored on foot. Polanco is one of the safest and most upscale neighborhoods in the city.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the Museo Nacional de Antropología (National Museum of Anthropology) in Chapultepec — considered one of the greatest museums in the world. Highlights include the Aztec Sun Stone, the Mayan Room, and the Olmec colossal heads. Hire a private expert guide for a curated 2–3 hour premium tour focused on Mesoamerican civilizations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Bosque de Chapultepec, one of the largest urban parks in the Americas. Visit Chapultepec Castle (Castillo de Chapultepec), a stunning hilltop palace with sweeping panoramic views of the city and remarkable historical murals inside. Leisurely return to the hotel for final packing and relaxation. Optional: indulge in a traditional temazcal (pre-Hispanic steam ceremony) or spa treatment at the hotel or a nearby luxury wellness center.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a premium restaurant of choice — consider Sud 777 in the Pedregal neighborhood for innovative contemporary Mexican cuisine in a stunning architectural setting, or return to a favorite from the trip. End the evening with a final mezcal nightcap at a rooftop bar overlooking the illuminated Centro Histórico.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final hotel breakfast — savor café de olla, pan dulce, and a classic Mexican egg dish such as huevos a la mexicana.
meals.lunch: Contramar, a legendary Mexico City seafood institution in Colonia Roma, famous for its grilled whole fish (pescado a la talla) and vibrant atmosphere — a true local institution beloved by chefs worldwide.
meals.dinner: Sud 777 or a return visit to a top pick from the week. Request a chef's tasting menu for a memorable farewell dining experience. Toast with a premium añejo tequila or rare single-village mezcal.

day_by_day.notes: The Anthropology Museum is vast — a private guide ensures you see the highlights without fatigue. Confirm departure logistics with the hotel concierge the evening before. Allow at least 3 hours for airport transfer and check-in for international flights.
